# Realty Income, Macro, and Bitcoin Deep Dive Analysis

Report 131 | Published 2024-03-05 | Evaluated 2026-11-07

[Original member article](https://www.lynalden.com/premium-2024-3-5/) | [Article index](README.md) | [Structured review](../data/reviews/131.json)

Liquidity, bitcoin adoption, and net-lease valuation.

Directionally constructive bitcoin and gold views had subsequent support. The strongest analytical distinction is marginal supply versus issuance. Realty Income expected returns and broad causal stories remain less testable than the price direction; ten-year resilience is unresolved.

**Coverage:** Read all blocks and image inventory. Covered macro, China, bitcoin cycle, Realty Income and gold; excluded routine allocations and disclaimers.

## Claims

### 131-C01

**Liquidity offsets limit broad tailwinds.**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Mixed |
| Type | explanation |
| Horizon | Not specified |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | net-liquidity-offsets |
| Source blocks | 9, 13, 16 |
| Thesis family | net-liquidity-offsets |

A reproducible domestic approximation is effectively flat between January 3 and February 28: $6.203 tn versus $6.212 tn. This supports the contemporaneous offset description. Marginal global risk capital and subsequent asset sensitivity do not follow uniquely from that identity.

**Direction:** Observed components differ.

**Timing:** No fixed deadline stated.

**Mechanism:** Evaluate the explanation separately from subsequent price direction.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Next test:** Test marginal asset sensitivity separately; reconstruct exact-day TGA if exact proxy values matter.

**Outcome evidence:**

- [WALCL observations](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/WALCL) | FRED / originating agency | 2026-11-07 | Verified in the audit

Calculation in millions: WALCL - WTREGEN -1000*RRPONTSYD. Jan 3 2024=6202700; Feb 28=6212100. WTREGEN is weekly average, making this approximate rather than exact daily TGA. Latest downloaded vintage, capped November 7; not original-release vintage.

- [WTREGEN observations](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/WTREGEN) | FRED / originating agency | 2026-11-07 | Verified in the audit

Treasury cash component used in disclosed approximate calculation. Latest downloaded vintage, capped November 7; not original-release vintage.

- [RRPONTSYD observations](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/RRPONTSYD) | FRED / originating agency | 2026-11-07 | Verified in the audit

Reverse repo component converted from billions to millions. Latest downloaded vintage, capped November 7; not original-release vintage.

### 131-C09

**Existing holders set marginal supply.**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Right |
| Type | explanation |
| Horizon | Not specified |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | bitcoin-liquid-supply |
| Source blocks | 53, 58, 64 |
| Thesis family | bitcoin-liquid-supply |

New issuance is only one source of tradable coins. The stock can transact repeatedly; price clears willingness to buy and sell, so comparing ETF demand only with mined supply is incomplete.

**Direction:** Supported for the defined proposition.

**Timing:** No fixed deadline stated.

**Mechanism:** Narrow deductive identity only; no empirical forecasting credit.

**Reviewer confidence:** high

**Deductive assessment:**

- Existing coins can be transferred
- Positive holder willingness to sell at some prices

Available sell flow at price p equals newly issued coins offered plus existing inventory offered; issuance is therefore not an upper bound on market supply.

**Outcome evidence:**

No independent outcome source is recorded. Any deductive assessment is identified separately.
